claim: BIP 448 makes a k-party channel (hyperedge) practical: one aggregate signature per state, later states replace earlier ones without per-state penalty data.
environment: patched regtest only; BIP 448 is not active on any public network

implementation.activation: bitcoin-rs --network regtest --bip448 (VerifyFlags::BIP448, default off; non-regtest networks refuse the switch)

results.includes: BIP 446 basics.json and script_assets_test.json vectors, 19 BIP 340 vectors through CSFS, existing Core script vectors

e2e_three_party_channel.update_leaf: OP_TEMPLATEHASH / OP_INTERNALKEY / OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK rebindable update per the BIP 448 LN-Symmetry description
rejections: stale state-2 update over state 3: script-verify-flag-failed
settlement before the CSV delay: non-BIP68-final
same spend without --bip448: mempool script-verify-flag-failed (opcodes stay OP_SUCCESS)

not_covered: fee anchors and fee bumping on update transactions
interpretation_notes: CSFS with a non-empty signature requires exactly 64 bytes (BIP 348 does not state a length rule).
CSFS unknown public key types follow BIP 342's DISCOURAGE_UPGRADABLE_PUBKEYTYPE policy.
